scope: Read-only saved native startup boundary plus later Linux memory snapshot; no allocation or cache modifications.
interpretation: Async live memory is close to the checkpoint payload; weights omitted by target-only loading and runtime/cache allocations prevent exact equality.
Only about94MiB of the async pool is reserved but reclaimable at the saved boundary; graph current memory is0.

OS MemAvailable substantially exceeds CUDA available. Later MemFree is near the low CUDA free value, while tens ofGiB are file cache; this accounts for most apparent missing memory without asserting exact file ownership.
File-cache pages can be reclaimable without appearing as already free in CUDA memory queries. No cache was dropped, and no hidden40GiB live model allocation was found in saved allocator telemetry.
Later OS snapshot is not simultaneous with the saved boundary; do not use it for an exact byte-balanced physical memory accounting.
